Management Plan
2026
Directorate-General for Internal Market,
Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
1

PART 1. Introduction
The Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs (DG GROW) is
responsible for strengthening the EU’s Single Market and reinforcing the competitiveness of European
industry.
We remove barriers in the Single Market so that citizens and companies, in particular SMEs,
can benefit from the scale and depth of a large unified market based on a transparent
rulebook. We strive to create an enabling environment for European industry and bolster
competitiveness by derisking investment, strengthening the resilience of EU economy and
addressing strategic dependencies. We facilitate access to funding and to global markets
for EU companies and we strive for the simplification of their business environment.
Strategic planning and programming are the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the political
priorities set out in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general objectives. This
process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the actions of all
Commission services with the strategic vision of this mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for 2025-2029 in
(management plan 2025). This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives and indicators to
measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning and reporting on
performance throughout the period.
The 2026 Management Plan sets out what DG GROW intends to deliver in 2026 to contribute to these
multiannual objectives (Part 2) and describes how DG GROW will contribute to the common objective
of building a modern and sustainable public administration (Part 3). The main outputs with their
indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG GROW.

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
In 2026, we will contribute to achieving four General Objectives of the Commission for 2025-2029,
namely General Objective 1: sustainable prosperity and competitiveness, General Objective 2: a new
era for European defence and security, and General Objective 6: a global Europe: leveraging our power
and partnerships.
General Objective 1: A new plan for Europe’s sustainable
prosperity and competitiveness
Specific objective 1.1 – Businesses, from SMEs to large firms, find
it easier to invest
Initiatives linked to regulatory simplification and burden reduction
European Product Act (2)
We will put forward the European Product Act (EPA) – a comprehensive proposal to modernise the
EU’s product legislative framework by bringing together its three core pillars: standardisation,
conformity assessment, and market surveillance. The EPA will enhance competitiveness by providing
a framework covering the entire products’ lifecycle and leveraging synergies between existing
legislation, to build a simple and efficient Single Market for goods. The EPA will also update the New
Legislative Framework (NLF) to reflect technological innovation in digitalisation and circularity.
In parallel, the EPA will update the EU rules on market surveillance and product compliance. As part
of the upcoming EPA, we will explore the feasibility of a horizontal legal framework for a Digital
Product Passport to ensure better traceability and authenticity of goods entering the EU.
European Biotech Act II
The EU Biotech Act II will reaffirm biotechnology as a cross-sectoral strategic technology, essential to
Europe’s competitiveness, resilience, and clean and digital transitions. The main objective is to create
a true level playing field within the Single Market, removing fragmentation and ensuring that
innovative biotech products and processes can access the market speedily and circulate freely across
the Union. The scope of the proposal will be determined in alignment with the Biotech Act I to avoid
overlaps and ensure synergies.
Public Procurement Act
We will put forward proposal on the revision of the Public Procurement Directives to modernise the
EU public procurement framework and reduce administrative burden for public buyers and economic
operators. Given the size of the EU procurement market, equivalent to about 15% of the EU GDP,
there is a clear potential in efficiently channelling investment in line with EU strategic priorities. The
(2) Initiatives that are part of the 2026 CWP are marked with this icon
5

reform will make public procurement part of the EU strategic investment agenda based on
simplification of existing public procurement procedures while improving transparency to avoid
irregular practices. It will furthermore support European lead markets and ensure investment in
Europe by incorporating European preferences for strategic products and sectors. It will also aim to
support environmentally and socially sustainable public procurement as well as the procurement of
innovative solutions.
Revision of the e-Invoicing Directive
The Single Market Strategy announced a legislative revision of the electronic invoicing in public
procurement rules. In 2026, we will put forward the relevant proposal. The objective is to increase
harmonisation of e-Invoicing rules across the EU leading to more uniformity on the use of e-Invoicing
by EU businesses, including SMEs, and ensuring its consistent use in public procurement throughout
the EU. Further harmonisation is expected to reduce costs for businesses, increase cross border
transactions, and ultimately foster their competitiveness in the Single Market.
Circular Economy Act
In 2026, as part of the Clean Industrial Deal, we will work, in cooperation with DG ENV, towards the
adoption of the Circular Economy Act (CEA), contributing to the ambition to make the EU the world
leader on circular economy by 2030. The CEA aims to increase circularity, leveraging the full potential
of the Single Market and promoting more sustainable production, circular economy business models
and supporting decarbonisation. The Act will facilitate the free movement of ‘circular’ products,
secondary raw materials and waste, including e-waste. It will also increase the supply of high-quality
recycled materials and stimulate demand for these materials in the EU.
Industrial Accelerator Act
In 2026, we will continue the implementation of initiatives described in the Communication “Delivering
on the Clean Industrial Deal”(3). Upcoming implementation measures, such as the Industrial
Accelerator Act, will allow for the creation of lead markets to boost demand for clean and Made in
EU industrial products in key strategic sectors and technologies, to speed up
industrial decarbonisation projects, while strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and economic
resilience .
REACH Revision
Following the European Chemicals Industry Action Plan and proposals for simplification of certain
requirements and procedures for chemical products (Omnibus VI), we will put forth a targeted revision
of REACH focusing on three main pillars: 1) modernisation, 2) simplification and digitalisation, 3)
enforcement, while continuing to ensure a high level of protection of human health and environment.
EU Industrial Maritime Strategy
In 2026, DG GROW together with DG MOVE will present a new Industrial maritime strategy to enhance
the competitiveness, sustainability and resilience of Europe’s maritime manufacturing sector. The
strategy is a flagship action of the Competitiveness Compass and will outline measures to boost
innovation, investment and a global level playing field.

Implementation dialogues and reality checks
EU Product Act
The preparation of the EU Product Act will be accompanied by reality checks with relevant
stakeholders.
Major public consultations
• Revision of the Market Surveillance Regulation
• Revision of the New Legislative Framework
• Revision of Public Procurement Framework
• Revision of the e-Invoicing Directive
Major implementation activities and enforcement actions
We drive the implementation of Industrial Policy with our stakeholder networks, notably the Industrial
Forum, the Enterprise Europe Network and the European Cluster Cooperation Platform.
Access to finance
We will continue to steer public and private investment with guarantee facilities and equity co-
investments under the SME window of InvestEU, as well as with capacity building and advisory
services to implementing partners under the EU Advisory Hub. We will continue disseminating
information on financial support under InvestEU by promoting the ‘Access2Finance’ portal and
promote match making of investors and project promoters through the InvestEU Portal. The EU
Finance Days in 2026 will have a focus on competitiveness and sustainability, including on the future
European Competitiveness Fund.
Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEIs)
The Joint European Forum for Important Projects of Common European Interest (JEF-IPCEI), co-
chaired by DG GROW and DG COMP, will continue working on the identification of candidates for new
IPCEIs, notably in the critical raw materials and clean connected autonomous vehicle strategic sectors,
while at the same time improving and simplifying the IPCEIs process from set-up to implementation.
Through the Design Support Hub, DG GROW will continue to provide expertise to Member States
working on IPCEI candidates (notably in circular advanced materials, nuclear and biotechnologies)
endorsed by the JEF-IPCEI and currently in the design phase.
7

Other implementation activities and enforcement actions
As highlighted in the Single Market Strategy, improved enforcement of the Single Market regulatory
framework is key to ensuring the Single Market exists as a tangible reality for businesses and citizens.
We will continue to play a crucial role as guardian in this process, including taking infringement
proceedings, and acting in parallel with other designated actors in implementation and enforcement.
Other major output
2026 Annual Single Market and Competitiveness Report
The 2026 Annual Single Market and Competitiveness report will assess the functioning of the Single
Market and the state of Europe’s competitiveness along the axes of the Competitiveness Compass -
closing the innovation gap, decarbonising our economy, and reducing dependencies. The report will be
based on a revised set of Key Performance Indicators, and it will monitor progress considering the
implementation of the Competitiveness Compass, the Clean Industrial Deal and the Single Market
Strategy.
2026 Annual Progress Report on Simplification, Implementation, and Enforcement
The Report will highlight key achievements and ongoing actions, including enforcement efforts, to
ensure the effective application of EU legislation for the Single Market. It will highlight progress in
ongoing initiatives to simplify the acquis and streamline processes and outline future avenues for
continued simplification and impactful implementation.
Roadmap Towards Phasing Out Animal Testing for Chemical Safety Assessments
We will put forward the roadmap towards phasing out animal testing for chemical safety assessments
as announced in response to the European Citizens’ Initiative “Save Cruelty-Free Cosmetics”. It will
provide a strategic plan to guide the progressive and scientifically robust transition towards non-
animal approaches for chemical safety assessments using innovative biotechnological and
computational methods offering potential to increase cost-efficiency and to accelerate safety
assessments as well as time-to-market.
Pending proposals with the co-legislator
• Proposal for a Regulation on circularity requirements for vehicle design and on management
of end-of-life vehicles
• Proposal for a Regulation for simplification of certain requirements and procedures for
chemical products (Omnibus VI)

• Proposals for Supplementary Protection Certificates for plant protection products, medicinal
products, and amending regulations
• Proposal for a Directive on mitigating measures available for small and medium sized
enterprises to small mid-cap enterprises and further simplifying measures (Omnibus IV)
• Proposal for a Regulation on mitigating measures available for small and medium sized
enterprises to small mid-cap enterprises and further simplification measures (Omnibus IV)

Specific objective 1.2 – Investment is mobilised to finance
competitiveness
Major implementation activities and enforcement actions
InvestEU Programme
InvestEU aims to mobilise at least EUR 372 billion of additional investment through EU budget
guarantees. An additional EUR 55 billion is expected to be mobilised once the Omnibus II (4) is
adopted. DG GROW will continue to negotiate, amend and sign Guarantee Agreements with existing
and new Implementing Partners to fully allocate the EU guarantee. We are also planning to conclude
further Contribution Agreements for Member State compartments. Additional Agreements with the
selected partners for the Advisory Hub are expected to be signed and the InvestEU Portal will continue
to cooperate with its existing partners.
European Competitiveness Fund
The European Competitiveness Fund (ECF) is set to become a cornerstone of the Multiannual Financial
Framework 2028-2034 (MFF), featuring a substantial allocation of EUR 234 billion. In combination with
Horizon Europe (EUR 175 billion), it draws together the firepower at EU level of EUR 409 billion to
accelerate the development, scaling-up, and manufacturing of strategic technologies in Europe. This figure
represents 21% of the future EU budget and has the potential to generate an even greater impact through
its extensive array of financing tools and guarantees. The Fund will provide a wide financial toolbox,
including grants, procurement as well as budgetary guarantees and financial instruments under the ECF
InvestEU instrument.
Battery Booster Facility
The Battery Booster Facility is to mobilise EUR 1.5 billion from the Innovation Fund in financing to support
European battery cell producers during the ramp-up phase. Support will be provided through performance-
linked financial instruments such as interest-free loans. These will be provided in instalments and will be
performance-based, linked to the achievement of specific milestones. The first instalment of support is
aimed at reaching selected companies in 2026. Additionally, of the EUR 1.8 billion of financing set aside
for the Battery Booster, up to EUR 300 million will be used to support Critical Raw Materials projects crucial
to the battery value chain, notably lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese and graphite.
Pending proposals with the co-legislators
• Proposal for a Regulation on combating late payment in commercial transactions
(4) COM (2025) 84 final

Specific objective 1.3 – The Single Market is more integrated
New policy initiatives:
Short term rentals
As announced in the European Affordable Housing Plan, we will contribute to the work of the
Commission’s Housing Task Force, by putting forward a new legislative initiative on short-term rentals
as part of an Affordable Housing Act, to complement Regulation 2024/1028, and to enable public
authorities to take a set of justified and proportionate measures, particularly in areas of housing
stress.
Territorial Supply Constraints
As announced in the Single Market Strategy (5), we will develop tools to act against unjustified
Territorial Supply Constraints to cover situations beyond those captured by competition law. The
objective of this process is to determine the most suitable tools to address the issue appearing on
the ‘Terrible Ten’ list of the most harmful barriers to the Single Market.
Initiatives linked to regulatory simplification and burden reduction
EU Delivery Act
We will propose a new EU Delivery Act to replace the Postal Services Directive and the Cross-border
Parcels Regulation. The current postal regulatory framework is outdated. The new EU rules on postal
services will focus on delivery as a service and will ensure that people and businesses can receive
deliveries throughout the EU at affordable prices, while promoting fair competition on delivery
markets and increasing consumer protection.
Construction Services Act
We will take an initiative relating to construction services, closely aligned with the Single Market
Strategy, which called for a new sectoral policy approach to the Single Market for services,
complementing the existing horizontal policy approach of the Services Directive. This provides a new
dynamic, particularly for the services sectors which are the most relevant for the twin transitions and
could bring the highest economic added value. This initiative will contribute to the Affordable Housing
Plan and the European Strategy for Housing Construction.
Evaluations and fitness checks - part of the stress testing of the EU acquis
• Evaluation of mutual recognition of goods
• Evaluation of recreational craft
• Evaluation of the Geo-Blocking Regulation
• Evaluation of Trademark Implementation

Implementation dialogues and reality checks
EU Delivery Act
The preparation of the EU Delivery Act will be accompanied in the first half of 2026 by an
implementation dialogue to feed into the process and reflection. The aim will be to identify and
confirm obstacles relating to existing EU postal rules and their implementation, and to explore and
discuss concrete suggestions on policy options.
SME Policy
An implementation dialogue on SME Policy is planned for the second half of 2026. The dialogue will
address the role of SMEs in the resilience of strategic supply chains and gain insights into sector-
specific SME perspectives. It will explore EU, local support and improvement, as well as address
regulatory, financial, and cross-border integration challenges.
Major public consultations
• EU Delivery Act
• Construction Services Act
Major implementation activities and enforcement actions
Single Market Strategy
The majority of legislative actions in the Single Market Strategy are to be put forward by the
Commission in 2026, with some actions already implemented in the course of 2025. The Single
Market Strategy is meant to address the ten most harmful Single Market barriers, known as the
‘Terrible Ten’. We will continue to coordinate the implementation of the Single Market Strategy
throughout 2026.
Single Market Enforcement Taskforce (SMET)
We will drive the work of the Single Market Enforcement Taskforce (SMET) as a cooperative platform
where Member States and the European Commission work together on removing or reducing barriers
in the Single Market.
We will focus on following up on SMET projects where efforts have not been successful and will
organise SMET annual high-level meeting to cater for political reinforcement to further empower
SMET and will continue working on its currently active projects while exploring new areas for potential
SMET projects. Finally, SMET will continue strengthening further cooperation with stakeholders,
especially with a view of the implementation process for addressing the Terrible Ten barriers.
Guidelines on the implementation of the Forced Labour Regulation
As foreseen by article 11 of the Forced Labour Regulation, we will issue guidelines by June 2026, in
consultation with relevant stakeholders. They will include guidance for economic operators on due
diligence and engaging with competent authorities, guidance for competent authorities on conducting
investigations, and guidance for stakeholders on submitting information, while minimising burdens
on administrations and companies.
11

SOLVIT
SOLVIT is a network of national civil servants dealing with Single Market complaints of EU citizens
and businesses. In 2026, we will continue to address systemic issues through SOLVIT cases, allocate
resources and strengthen the cooperation with other DGs to improve information exchange. With a
new IMI application to be rolled out in 2026, we will undertake migration from old IMI application to
the new one and continue the close monitoring of the cases submitted by businesses, in particular
under the Mutual Recognition of Goods regulation.
Other major output
Revision of Textile Labelling Regulation
The revision will aim at modernising current fibre composition rules and introducing a fully
harmonised single label, both physical and digital, encompassing all the relevant labelling information,
as announced in the Single Market Strategy of 2025.
EU Designs and Models Package
In July 2026, Phase 2 of the new EU Designs and Models Package developed by DG GROW will be
implemented. The reform mainly affects the procedural practice of the European Union Intellectual
Property Office (EUIPO) in the design representation regime, aiming to adapt the more than twenty-
year-old system to the realities of digital business models and emerging technologies, such as 3D
printing, virtual designs and modular products.
Unitary Patent Report
In 2026, we will present to the European Parliament and the Council a report on the operation of
Regulation 1257/2012 implementing enhanced cooperation around the creation of Unitary Patent
Protection. The report will take stock and assess the functioning of the Unitary patent system after
the third year of its entry into force in June 2023.
Pending proposals with the co-legislator
• Proposal for a Directive amending Directives as regards digitalisation and common
specifications (Omnibus IV)
• Proposal for a Regulation amending Directives as regards digitalisation and common
specifications (Omnibus IV)
• Proposal for a Regulation on a public interface connected to the Internal Market Information
System for the declaration of posting of workers.
• Proposal for a Regulation establishing the Single Market and Customs Programme for the
period 2028-2034 and repealing Regulations (EU) 2021/444, (EU) 2021/690, (EU) 2021/785,
(EU) 2021/847 and (EU) 2021/1077.
12

General Objective 2: A new era for European defence and
security
Specific Objectives 2.1: EU dependencies are reduced
New policy initiatives
Critical Raw Materials Centre
Critical Raw Materials (CRM) are vital for European industry. However, Europe’s heavy reliance on
concentrated import sources creates geopolitical vulnerabilities. In line with the Clean Industrial Deal
and building on the experience of implementing the Critical Raw Materials Act and the 47 Strategic
projects selected so far, we will establish a CRM Centre to address the lack of secure and reliable
access to raw materials for European industries, and their limited resilience to withstand supply chain
disruptions. It will focus on strategic stockpiling, joint purchasing, supply chain monitoring and
investment in raw materials sources outside and inside the EU.
Major public consultations:
• Critical Raw Materials Centre
Major implementation activities and enforcement actions
The Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Package
The Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA), adopted in October 2024, will come into
effect on 29 May 2026. As part of the IMERA implementation activities, we will adopt an implementing
act setting out detailed arrangements for a contingency planning framework regarding crisis
preparedness, cooperation, exchange of information and crisis communication for the internal market
vigilance and emergency modes. We will also organise a crisis simulation exercise to stress test IMERA
as part of the enforcement efforts.
General Objective 6: A global Europe: Leveraging our power and
partnerships
Specific Objective 6.1: More opportunities are generated for EU
industry and services in the global markets
New policy initiatives
Supply Chain Resilience
Supply chain diversification is crucial for business resilience, helping companies to mitigate risks amid
global trade uncertainties. As part of the EU’s industrial and competitiveness agenda and its economic
security strategy, we will aim to reinforce supply chain cooperation through Industrial Policy Dialogues
(with Japan, the Republic of Korea, China, Taiwan, Ukraine and for the first time, Canada), mobilising
business networks to leverage mutual complementarities.
13

The EU-Japan Centre for Industrial cooperation will participate in this effort. We will develop cooperation
globally to pursue opportunities for market integration and business cooperation.
We will reinforce supply chain complementarities with candidate countries, including Western Balkans
countries, Ukraine and Moldova by implementing “Single Market Highways”. We will assist enlargement
countries, including the new candidate countries - Ukraine and Moldova -, and support the implementation
of the Growth Plan for the Western Balkans. We will deliver on the Agreement on Conformity Assessment
and Acceptance (ACAA) of industrial products with Ukraine. And we will continue the work on an ACAA with
Moldova and Serbia. We will also participate in defining conditions for foreign investments to positively
contribute to Europe’s competitiveness in key strategic sectors such as automotive and batteries. We will
pursue the reciprocal opening of procurement markets in third countries and negotiating trade agreements
aiming at mitigating protectionist or discriminatory measures.
Other major output
To reach the objectives of the Critical Raw Materials Act, the EU has concluded Strategic Partnerships
covering raw materials value chains with third countries, as part of its strategy for ensuring a secure and
sustainable supply of critical raw materials, with 14 partnerships so far. In 2026, it is planned that DG
GROW will work towards a Memorandum of Understanding which will set a strategic partnership with
Brazil - one of the most important global producers of many critical raw materials.
Major implementation activities and enforcement actions
Foreign Subsidies Regulation
We will continue to pursue the enforcement of the procurement pillar of the Foreign Subsidies Regulation
(FSR), thereby contributing to a level playing field in EU public procurement by addressing the distortive
effects of foreign subsidies. Where required and justified, both DG GROW and DG COMP will open ex officio
investigations when Commission action is warranted on its own initiative. DG GROW’s sectoral focus and
economic intelligence will help identify critical areas where such investigations are particularly relevant to
ensure fair competition and a level playing field within the Union.
Foreign Subsidies Review Report and FSR Guidelines
Together with DG COMP, we will publish our first FSR Guidelines. A meeting of national contact points will
also take place in January 2026 to strengthen cooperation with Member States and support effective
enforcement. In addition, an FSR review report will be prepared, leading to simplification and burden-
reduction measures, for publication in July 2026.
14

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular, it
ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable levels
through cost-effective controls.
DG GROW has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an ongoing
basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all internal control
principles.
A. Human resource management
To achieve its ambitious objectives, human resources management remains a top priority for DG
GROW, which is committed to leveraging its skilled, motivated, and dedicated staff.
In 2026, we will continue to analyse the workload of each Unit and to rebalance the human resources
via internal redeployments, within the current resource constraints. We will help managers identify
talents to fill their needs more rapidly and to keep their talents who passed a competition or the
certification procedure.
On gender equalities policies, DG GROW will continue to maintain the balance at all management
levels as referenced in Annex 2:
• On 19 November 2025, 47% of middle management was female (4 posts were vacant), and
58.33% of Deputy Head of Unit’s post were held by female colleagues (1 post was vacant);
the aim is to sustain a minimum of 50% by 2029.
• By appointing five female Heads of Unit as Deputies to Directors as of May 1, 2025, DG GROW
achieved gender balance goals with 55% female representation and the aim is to maintain
this balance.
• In November 2025, DG GROW’s female senior managers represented 61.5% of that category.
DG GROW remains committed to fostering women's career development through participation in its
own Female Talent Development Programme, developed in collaboration with DGs COMP, ECFIN, and
FISMA.
The staff engagement index at DG GROW surpassed the Commission's average in 2023. The target
for 2029 is to maintain or improve the high level of engagement.
DG GROW will also continue to work on its internal communication to enhance staff engagement, with
initiatives such as participatory meetings, including all-staff meetings led by the Director General,
Directors’ debriefings, and presentations by colleagues on policy files and DG services, as referenced
in Annex 2.
15

Additionally, DG GROW will continue offering well-being activities. In 2026, we plan expanding
engagement activities, such as an all-staff video, podcasts, ‘getting to know each other’ events, to
reinforce the cohesion between Brussels and Luxembourg’s sites and promote a dynamic and
supportive workplace culture.
B. Digital transformation and data management
Local Digital Transformation in DG GROW is fully aligned with the Commission’s strategic priorities,
its digital strategy and the findings we gathered, both through surveys on digital skills and visits to
the directorates and units.
In 2026 we will continue to work towards the smooth functioning of a digital and data driven
Single Market, by further developing and modernising our IT portfolio of strategically important
systems, to deliver on simplification of the acquis, reducing administrative burden and enabling a
seamless flow of data in the Single Market. Building on top of the success of GROW’s AI Pilot on
complaints handling with Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) that is expected to be integrated in the corporate
solution for complaints’ handling THEMIS, there are several use cases that will be developed in 2026,
the proactive detection of violations of GROW acquis, prevention of potentially disproportionate
regulatory environments and extending smart search, summarization and drafting functionalities of
AI to SOLVIT centres. Existing systems like Single Digital Gateway (SDG), Public Procurement Data
Space (PPDS), InvestEU and Technical Regulation Information System (TRIS) will be enhanced with
new AI capabilities while newly developed systems will, where possible, have AI integrated in their
workflows.
We will intensify activities that aim to raise the level of digital skills for all colleagues, including
the management. Apart from improving the use of collaborative tools like Teams and SharePoint
Online, we will focus on enabling colleagues to get knowledge and skills to make the best use of the
corporate AI tools, such as GPT@EC and the forthcoming AI@EC platform. This work will be managed
locally by our GROW AI Champions Network and occasionally supported by the central services.
Our systems will utilise more open-source solutions, implement more reusable solutions, be hosted
on the cloud, and align with EU sovereignty principles whenever possible. The work on business
processes automation will progress and we expect to see the first results in improving efficiency by
the end of the year.
DG GROW will remain committed to maintaining its leading position as far as cybersecurity of its IT
portfolio is concerned.
The activities mentioned above constitute the Digital Transformation Roadmap of DG GROW.
Data management
In 2025, DG GROW has an established maturity in data management practices which we aim to
advance in 2026. To achieve this, we will encode systematically new assets in the EC Data Catalogue
and ensure yearly updates.
Currently, ownership and responsibilities are in developing stage, aiming to reach in 2026 the
level in which responsibilities of data owners and stewards are clearly assigned, clarified, and
16

documented for all data assets. To support this transition, we will conduct awareness sessions with
Data Owners and seek support from the EC Data Advisory.
DG GROW has established principles of data quality and FAIRness (6) in 2025 targeting an
advanced level in 2026. DG GROW will publish additional data assets in the open data portal, continue
its efforts on interoperability, and raise awareness to improve data quality.
Regarding data skills, DG GROW is developing data-related competencies. In 2026, our target is to
establish these skills, by identifying learning paths and sharing information via GROW Talks.
Additionally, as part of the Internal Market Family coordination, a data maturity survey was
performed. Its results give a more detailed view in terms of the above criteria and are available upon
request.
Data Protection
DG GROW Data Protection Coordinator (DPC) will focus on the needs of every type of actor in the practical
implementation of Data Protection, promoting the use of unit inventories of processing operations. This
will improve continuous compliance monitoring and in particular the implementation of the Commission's
Data Protection Action Plan (C(2018) 7432 final). We will also continue to ensure that GROW IT systems
and websites comply with data protection rules, including security aspects.
Throughout 2026, we will map the implementation per Unit (to target awareness actions). We will
focus on ensuring timely completion of new records, together with the corresponding privacy
statements, in the case of newly identified processing activities, as well as timely review of published
records of processing activities.
C. Sound financial management
In 2026, DG GROW will continue to ensure the sound and efficient management of its financial
resources, and to maintain effective internal control, risk management and accounting reporting. The
main focus will be on effective budget implementation, effective programme governance, as well as
simplified, harmonised and digital working methods using the available corporate tools. The dedicated
SharePoint space allows easy access for all staff to information on financial and internal control
matters.
We will continue to focus on implementing - through direct and indirect management - the
programmes for which DG GROW: 1) is fully responsible (InvestEU), 2) ensures coordination at
programme level and manages activities in the area of SMEs, European standardisation, Internal
Market and Market Surveillance (Single Market Programme), 3) is co-chair of Cluster 4 on Digital,
Industry and Space (Horizon Europe). The Executive Agencies EISMEA and HaDEA, as well as
Decentralised agencies and EUIPO will continue to support the implementation of DG GROW
programmes. We will also continue to ensure coordination with the EIB, EIF, EBRD and other European
and International Financial Institutions for the implementation of InvestEU. With reference to the
European Competitiveness Fund, under the lead of DG BUDG, HR and SG, DG GROW will contribute to
the cost-benefit analysis (CBA) for the direct programme implementation 2028-2034. The outcome
of the corporate measurement on 11 standard financial indicators common to all Commission
(6) “FAIRness” is a data management term describing the extent of ‘findability, accessibility, interoperability and
reusability’ of data.

services (7) showed that DG GROW performs according to expected standards. DG GROW has ensured
excellent results in budget implementation for both commitment and payment appropriations and
also in other financial Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). DG GROW will also monitor internally its
financial performance on a monthly basis through KPIs, to ensure a sound and efficient financial
management and the follow-up of financial transactions.
Details about the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) pursued by DG GROW are provided in Annex 2
(on page 33). In particular, the effectiveness of the controls will be monitored by ensuring that both
the overall risk at payment and risk at closure remain below 1%. Efficiency will be ensured by
achieving 100% budget execution of commitment and payment appropriations in operational lines
and of commitment appropriations in administrative lines. Regarding the economy of controls, it will
be monitored that the overall estimated cost of controls remains under 5%.
DG GROW will continue to support the development and take-up of corporate digital tools, such as
eProcurement. DG GROW will pursue its efforts to maintain its effective internal control framework,
notably by implementing the updated internal control strategy. The reinforced supervision of the
executive agencies and external entities implementing DG GROW activities will be maintained
throughout 2026.
Audits on the activities of DG GROW are expected to be launched by ECA and IAS in 2026. Respective
recommendations for further improvements will be duly monitored and addressed on time ensuring
accountability and transparency. The IAS audit on “InvestEU” has been launched early 2025. In
addition, there are several on-going performance audits launched by ECA where DG GROW is either
the lead or an associated DG.
D. Fraud risk management
In the implementation of its Anti-fraud strategy, DG GROW organises, on a regular basis, trainings for
newcomers on ethics and anti-fraud. All information related to fraud risk management is published
on DG GROW’s Intranet. DG GROW is in the process of updating the Anti-Fraud strategy to ensure it
remains up to date, with the goal of adopting the revised version in 2026. The implementation of DG
GROW action plan is regularly monitored.
The main actions intended to be implemented by DG GROW in 2026, as indicated also in Annex 2 (on
page 33) include updating the Anti-Fraud strategy, providing at least one information session on
ethics and anti-fraud. Cooperation with OLAF and other Commission services and Executive Agencies
will be enhanced to contribute to the implementation of the Commission Anti-Fraud Strategy (CAFS)
through participation in the Commission’s Fraud Prevention and Detection Network (FPDNet).
Additionally, fraud awareness will be raised by updating the relevant section in the Intranet.

E. Sound environmental management
DG GROW remains committed to implementing the Communication and action plan on greening the
Commission.
In line with the Commission’s multiannual objective, DG GROW remains committed to minimising its
environmental and carbon footprint in support of climate neutrality by 2030. Staff are encouraged to
opt for hybrid or online meetings or limiting the number of participants on missions.
DG GROW will continue to work in close collaboration with the Commission Office for Infrastructure and
Logistics in Brussels (OIB) on the following: infrastructure (buildings, lifts, water fountains, waste
collection etc.); supplies, including stationery and meeting material; promoting environmentally
conscious behaviour (waste collection, biking, use of stairs), continuing its policy of alternating physical
and online expert meetings.
